newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria sees 60 billion cu metres gas exports 1997.
newsitem.headline: Algeria sees 60 billion cu metres gas exports 1997.

text.p: Algeria's energy minister said on Tuesday his country would export 60 billion cubic metres of natural gas next year.

The official Algerian news agency APS quoted Amar Makhloufi as telling the National Transitional Council in Algiers: "Algeria will export 60 billion cubic metres of natural gas in 1997 thanks to new projects."
This is three years before previous forecasts made by Algerian officials who had given the year 2000 as the target date for exports to reach this figure.

"Exports of natural gas have been in the order of 42 billion cubic metres in the course of this year, of which 50 percent were transported by gas carriers and 50 percent by way of gas pipelines," the minister added.

He stressed the solid achievements made in exporting gas towards Europe, linked last month by a second Algeria-Spain pipeline, before adding: "Algeria has been able to get into the European market while other countries have not been able to succeed despite their considerable gas reserves."
The minister gave no details of the "new projects" to lift the exports.
The National Transitional Council, an unelected body which acts as Algeria's parliament, has been debating the North African OPEC member's 1997 budget.
